question: Who was turned away at the door of the very first World Science Fiction Convention in 1939?
answer: Fans who would become the genre's professionals. The New York organisers, feuding with a rival club called the Futurians, barred several of its members, among them Frederik Pohl and Donald Wollheim. Pohl became a leading editor and novelist; Wollheim founded DAW Books. About 200 people attended the convention they were kept out of.
move: Today's gatekeepers often lock out tomorrow's owners of the gate.
reference: Harry Warner Jr., All Our Yesterdays: An Informal History of Science Fiction Fandom in the Forties, Advent Publishers, 1969
